title: Book One · Chapter 23: Wet Paper
story:
In the morning, Ronan finds a dark mark under the table.

It is the shape of his board. One corner is wet. He lifts Jun's paper. The wet corner stays on the board.

He stands very still. The paper feels soft between his fingers. His thumb goes through it.

He looks at the door. Mum is in the yard with Mrs Lan. Rain came under the kitchen door. Mum and Mrs Lan are looking at that wet place.

Ronan puts the torn piece down. Two other sheets have stuck together. He pulls them apart slowly. Part of one sheet tears off.

The three pieces of paper lie in a wet pile.

He could call Mum. She is only a few steps away. He can hear her asking Mrs Lan for an old cloth to stop the water.

Instead, he moves the wet paper behind the board. He puts a dry scrap on top. From the door, it looks like the work is still there.

Mum comes in to get his school bag.

"Is everything off that damp part?"

"Yes," he says.

He did move the paper. But it is wet now. He needs to tell Mum about that too.

At school, Leo asks about Jun's kite. Ronan says he didn't do much last night. Leo says he didn't either. He had to go with his mother to collect his little cousin.

"Maybe tomorrow will be dry," Leo says.

Ronan nods. Ronan thinks about tomorrow. He needs dry paper and more sticks. He also needs to tell Jun. He says nothing about it to Leo.

At break, Jun asks, "Can I see my kite after school?"

"Not today."

"Why?"

"Mum's busy."

That is true too. Mum is busy almost every afternoon. But that is not the main problem. Jun's paper is wet. Ronan still does not tell him.

He gets home. The wet paper smells bad. He carries it outside and lays the sheets on the dry step. The sun has come through the clouds. Perhaps the paper will become good again.

One edge curls up. The dark patches become pale. The holes stay holes.

Mrs Lan comes through with a bowl.

"Drying something?"

"Paper."

"I can see that. Do you need more paper?"

Ronan nods.

She puts her bowl down. "Wet paper can dry with wrinkles. You might still use part of it."

"All of it?"

"I cannot promise that."

She leaves him to it. He cuts a dry corner from one sheet. It is big enough for a small drawing. It isn't big enough for a kite.

Mum brings a shirt back to a customer. Then she comes home. Ronan is cutting the dry corner. Mum puts her bag down. "What happened?" she asks.

"The rain got it," Ronan says.

"When?"

"Last night."

"Did you know this morning?"

He presses the scissors closed. "Yes."

Mum sits on the step. She is quiet long enough for him to put the scissors away.

"You knew this morning," she says. "We had time to dry it then. But you did not tell me. I did not know you needed help."

Ronan brings the wet pile to her. He doesn't put the clean scrap on top this time. They put the good pieces in one pile. The torn pieces go in another. Mum can see all of it now. Ronan sits beside her. He stops trying to cover the holes.

---

重点表达：wrinkles＝皱褶；torn＝撕破的；wet＝湿的；holes＝洞。

理解问题：

1. 纸为什么湿了？
2. Ronan 隐瞒损失后，问题为什么更难处理？
